errors.description: The notch is unchanged from attempt 1. Traced at high magnification on the frame-right notch, the collar tip is still a hard sharp corner, the slot between collar tip and lapel is still a wide open wedge, and the gorge seam still runs dead straight from the notch up to the neck with no perceptible bow. None of the three shape corrections landed.
errors.expected: rounded hooking collar tip, narrow slot, visibly bowed gorge seam
errors.actual: sharp pointed collar tip, wide open wedge, ruler-straight gorge
errors.correction: make the collar tip finish in a small rounded curve like the end of a thumb rather than a point; make the gap between collar tip and lapel a narrow slit only a little wider than the cloth is thick; and bend the gorge seam into a shallow arc that is obviously not a straight line

errors.description: The V of the notch measures close to a right angle at its apex on both sides - wider even than the straight-notch sibling that sits next to this option in the same menu, and far wider than the tight notch the drawing shows.
errors.expected: a notch apex clearly tighter than a right angle and clearly tighter than the straight-notch sibling
errors.actual: an apex of roughly a right angle on both sides
errors.correction: close the notch down so the two edges lie much nearer to parallel: the wedge should look like a narrow slit cut into the edge, not an open mouth

errors.description: Because neither the notch shape nor the gorge curvature changed, the render still carries no feature that separates it from the other notch options on the same field. It remains a generic notch lapel.
errors.expected: a lapel a customer could pick out of the notch family by its curved gorge alone
errors.actual: a generic notch lapel indistinguishable from its neighbours
errors.correction: covered by the geometry and angle corrections

errors.description: The frame improved - the chest welt pocket is gone and the lapels now fill a proper share of the picture - but the jacket still runs off both side edges with no grey margin beside either lapel, and the model's chin is still above the collar.
errors.expected: left and right edges just outside each lapel's outer edge with a sliver of grey beyond; no chin in frame
errors.actual: jacket bleeds off both side edges; chin still visible
errors.correction: trim the side edges in a little further and drop the top edge to the base of the neck

lockedFeatures: the chest welt pocket is now correctly out of frame - keep it out
the lapels now fill a proper share of the picture - do not zoom back out
both lapels and the full collar in frame together, mirrored, straight on and dead level
no necktie and no pocket square, the white shirt collar showing plainly inside the V with the top shirt button open
the lapels tapering to a long deep V that converges low in the picture
the gorge high on the chest
one hand-worked keyhole buttonhole on the frame-right lapel only
fine tonal edge stitching along the lapel edge
zero numerals, arrows, leader lines, angle callouts, coloured guide marks or text anywhere in frame
notes:
ATTEMPT 2 vs /images/blueprints/factory/877a05ce586e__0689__Notch_with_high_gorge.jpg.

WHAT ATTEMPT 2 FIXED: composition only. The chest welt pocket is out of frame and the two lapels now occupy a proper share of the picture rather than a third of it.

WHAT IS STILL WRONG: every shape instruction was ignored. The collar tip is still a sharp spike where the drawing shows a small rounded hook; the notch slot is still a wide open wedge measuring near a right angle where the drawing shows a narrow slit; and the gorge seam is still a straight ruled line where the drawing bows it. This is the same generic notch lapel as attempt 1.

ROOT CAUSE: shape language buried in a long correction paragraph is losing to the model's very strong prior for 'notch lapel'. Attempt 3 must lead with the shape in the plainest possible physical terms - a rounded tip, a slit not a wedge, an arc not a line - and repeat it, rather than arguing about degrees.
